bounded_relationship.customer_downstream: Nova, contexto de computação e migração de instâncias.
bounded_relationship.supplier_upstream: Neutron, contexto de redes e vínculos de portas.
bounded_relationship.model_owner: Neutron controla o sub-recurso bindings, seu estado ativo/inativo e a ação activate, publicados por neutron-lib.
bounded_relationship.customer_control: Nova controla quando preparar o destino, iniciar a migração, ativar o vínculo e realizar rollback; o plano Neutron prevê atender os caminhos de rollback que Nova decidir implementar.

rows.mechanism: Nova precisava conhecer a ligação de rede do destino antes de mover a instância, preservando a ligação ativa na origem. A proposta do Neutron transformou essa necessidade em mudanças de API, modelo de dados e ML2, com responsável e plano de testes. O RFE correspondente registra Fix Released. A especificação aprovada do Nova prevê a adoção da API. No código atual, o conductor prepara as portas no destino; o cliente cria o binding por host e depois pede sua ativação. O Neutron cria o segundo vínculo como inativo, preserva o ativo e oferece a ação que troca a ligação selecionada. Assim, há uma necessidade downstream incorporada ao plano e ao contrato do fornecedor, além de chamadas entre serviços.
rows.limits: A interpretação Customer/Supplier vale para essa evolução histórica de port binding para migração. Não caracteriza toda a governança OpenStack nem prova execução em produção. A proposta Neutron encontrada está hoje em backlog/pike; não foi tratada como uma especificação Rocky aprovada. O pedido concluído, o plano aprovado do Nova e a implementação atual constituem as provas adicionais. A sintaxe publicada evoluiu: o código atual usa host, enquanto trechos antigos da proposta usam host_id.

28: Today, port binding occurs on the target compute host during migration,
29: considered now in the post_live_migration stage.  This, unfortunately, is
30: too late in the process as there are cases where Nova requires this
31: information in the pre_live_migration stage.  We simply cannot move the port
32: binding to the pre_live_migration stage as the original port binding would be
33: deleted, causing issues due to the instance being active still on the original
34: host.  Further details are contained in the 'Alternatives' section.

36: Problem Description
37: ===================
38: 
39: For live migration improvements, it is required that Neutron allows port
40: binding on the target compute host during the pre_live_migration stage, without
41: removing the original port binding on the source compute.
42: 
43: The proposal is to have a port binding on the source AND target compute hosts
44: where only one port binding is active.  After instance migration is complete,
45: the target port binding is activated and the source port binding is
46: deactivated, but not deleted.  The original port binding on the source compute

98: 
99: Proposed Change
100: ===============
101: 
102: For migration, Nova will require the port binding information from the target
103: compute during the pre_live_migration stage.  This can be achieved by allowing
104: a compute port to be bound to the migration source and the migration target
105: host.
106: 
107: This can be achieved by the following steps:
108: 
109: #1 Expand upon existing API entities under port, allowing CRUD bindings.
110: 
111: #2 Update ML2 to support the changes.
112: 
113: #3 Update the DB to support the changes.
114: 
115: Usage by Nova
116: -------------
117: 
118: Nova will utilize the expanded API, and the potential flow is as follows:
119: 
120: * pre_live_migration: Create the inactive binding for target host.
121: 
122: * live_migration_operation: Use information gathered from the inactive
123:   binding to modify the instance definition.
124: 
125: * live_migration_operation: Once the instance is active, set the inactive
126:   binding to active, and the previous active binding to inactive.
127: 
128: * post_live_migration: Remove the inactive binding on the source
129:   compute host.
130: 
131: .. image:: /images/pike/nova-live-migration-flow.png
132: 
133: * If rollback is performed after the instance is active on target: From a
134:   Neutron standpoint, if the binding is active on the target host, Nova will
135:   need to set the source binding back to active::
136: 
137:     PUT /v2.0/ports/{port_id}/bindings/{host_id}/activate
138: 
139: For more details on the Nova implementation , see the related Nova
140: Blueprint `[3]`_ and its Spec `[4]`_.  Neutron will not dictate the implemented
141: capabilities of Nova live migration and will support either path, to rollback
142: or to not rollback.

9: ===================================
10: 
11: Make use of Neutron's new port binding API in all cases where port binding
12: occurs. In the special case of move operations, the new API will allow us to
13: model both source and destination hosts having a port binding
14: which is not accounted for during live migration today.

91: Proposed change
92: ===============
93: 
94: There is no additional configuration for deployers.
95: The use of multiple bindings will be enabled automatically.
96: We decide whether to use the new or old API flow, if both compute nodes
97: support this feature and based on the available Neutron API extensions.
98: We cache extensions support in the usual way utilizing the existing
99: neutron_extensions_cache.
100: 
101: Note: The new neutron API extension will be implemented in the ml2 plugin
102: layer, above the ml2 driver layer so if the extension is exposed it will be
103: supported for all ml2 drivers. Monolithic plugins will have to implement
104: the extension separately and will continue to use the old workflow until
105: their maintainers support the new neutron extension.
106: 
107: The old interaction model should be removed when sufficient time has elapsed
108: for all neutron backends to support this model with an aim of completing this
109: in two cycles. We should keep this in mind in how the code is structured.
110: Given we are also looking at removing nova-network, we should see if this can
111: be added as a new set of network API calls, that are only for neutron, making
112: the existing calls needed for nova-network be no-ops for Neutron.
